advances:
The universal registered subgoal is false as currently worded because it
includes a genuine unmarked vertex of a triangular endpoint polygon, even
though such a vertex is not deletable while retaining a two-dimensional
endpoint.  On every counterclockwise triangular stratum,
\(\Delta_r=2|A_0|\), so the canonical release row is already \(-2\) times
the fixed endpoint-area row.  The exact rational realization below has
bounded two-dimensional \(Z,W\) codes, no active containment or intrinsic
capacity row, and the canonical dual stress
\[
y_{P_\varnothing}=-2,\qquad \lambda=0.
\]
Thus the projected cone exclusion fails exactly.

This is a counterexample only to the universal subgoal as it is currently
registered.  The realization does not impose the three \(2/9\)-crossings,
and deleting the chosen vertex leaves a segment.  It is therefore not a
counterexample to the intended three-crossing theorem fiber or to the
locked main theorem.  Restoring the former requirement
\[
\dim\operatorname{conv}(A_0\setminus\{a_r\})=2
\]
removes this counterexample.

proof:
For the three \(A_0\) vertices, the triples
\((f_1,f_2,f_3)\) are
\[
\left(-\frac{49}{100},-\frac{199}{200},\frac{97}{200}\right),
\quad
\left(\frac1{100},-\frac{199}{200},-\frac3{200}\right),
\quad
\left(-\frac{49}{100},-\frac{99}{200},-\frac3{200}\right).
\tag{21}
\]
Every coordinate is strictly greater than \(-1=L_i\), which proves the
\(P_\varnothing\) code and shows that every vertex is unmarked.
Shoelace gives \(|A_0|=1/8\).

For \(q_i=f_i+L_i=f_i-1\), the \(A_2\) vertex triples are
\[
\left(\frac1{100},-\frac1{100},-4\right),\quad
\left(-\frac1{100},\frac1{100},-4\right),\quad
\left(-1,-\frac{301}{100},\frac1{100}\right).
\tag{22}
\]
They lie strictly in \(Q_{23},Q_{13},Q_{12}\), respectively, and the
interior meets \(Q_{123}\).  Exact half-plane clipping and shoelace give
(4), so (3) is the complete positive \(Q\)-support.

The polygon \(K\) is the triangle
\[
x\le2,\qquad y\le2,\qquad x+y\ge-3.
\tag{23}
\]
Clipping it by \(f_i=0\) gives the seven values in (5).  Direct
substitution of the five vertices in (6) into (23) gives strict
inequalities, so every containment slack is positive.

In the \((S,T)=(f_1,f_2)\) coordinates, the five midpoint vertices are
exactly the five points in (6).  Each consecutive edge has a negative
\(S\)- or \(T\)-coordinate at an endpoint, so all five supports are
charging.  Intersecting those five support halfplanes with \(S,T\ge0\)
gives the triangle (9).  The active support pairs are exactly (10);
all other support evaluations are strict.  This proves the complete
two-dimensional \(Z,W\) codes, their equality, the absence of active
weak rows, and the zero capacity row in (11).

The only shared \(A_0,A_2\) ray is
\[
a_2-a_1=\left(-\frac12,\frac12\right),\qquad
q_1-q_0=\left(-\frac1{50},\frac1{50}\right).
\tag{24}
\]
Differentiating the fixed-code chamber shoelace formulas and (24) gives
the complete rational rows in (14).  The absent chamber rows and the
fixed cut-defined \(R_{123}\) row are identically zero.  Accepted fact `42e17c270e11ad3e` supplies the fixed-stratum release and
Farkas system used in (17)-(20), accepted fact `7e23b6c690af212a`
supplies the bounded \(Z,W\) capacity code and differential used in
(8)-(11), and accepted fact `ac38e37c661e844b` restricts the canonical
row list to the structural equalities, active intrinsic slacks, and
capacity row used in (13)-(15), including suppression of identically
zero defining rows.  This proves (13)-(15).

Finally, a counterclockwise triangle satisfies
\[
[a_0-a_2,a_1-a_0]=2|A_0|
\]
as an identity, not merely at the displayed point.  Differentiation
gives (17), and (18) gives (19) with a nonnegative inequality multiplier.
Right multiplication by any kernel basis gives (20).  Deleting \(a_0\)
leaves the segment \([a_1,a_2]\), so this is precisely the
nondeletable triangular case omitted from the wording of the registered
subgoal.

SageMath 10.8 over \(\mathbb Q\) was used only to audit the convex hull
list (6), the rational cell areas (4)-(5), the bounded code (9)-(10),
the rank of (14), and the displayed sparse row identity.  The decisive
dual certificate follows directly from the elementary triangle identity
\(\Delta_0=2|A_0|\).  No computational result is used to claim the three
\(2/9\)-crossings, an intended-fiber counterexample, or a counterexample
to the locked main theorem.
statement:
Work in coordinates
\[
f_1(x,y)=x,\qquad f_2(x,y)=y,\qquad f_3(x,y)=-1-x-y,
\qquad L_1=L_2=L_3=-1.
\]
Take the counterclockwise polygons
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(-49/100,-199/200),\ (1/100,-199/200),\
(-49/100,-99/200)\},\\
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(101/100,99/100),\ (99/100,101/100),\
(0,-201/100)\},\\
K=\operatorname{conv}\{&(-5,2),(2,-5),(2,2)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
All three vertices of \(A_0\) lie strictly in \(P_\varnothing\), and
\[
|A_0|=\frac18.
\tag{2}
\]
The positive \(Q\)-support is exactly the all-double support
\[
\{12,13,23,123\},
\tag{3}
\]
with
\[
q_{12}=\frac1{4\,010\,000},\qquad
q_{13}=\frac{401}{6\,040\,000},\qquad
q_{23}=\frac{401}{2\,020\,000},\qquad
q_{123}=\frac{9\,744\,640\,397}{244\,626\,040\,000}.
\tag{4}
\]
Every middle cell of \(K\) is positive:
\[
r_1=r_2=r_3=r_{12}=r_{13}=r_{23}=4,
\qquad r_{123}=\frac12.
\tag{5}
\]

The midpoint body \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\) has the counterclockwise merged-fan
list
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
j&b_j&(\iota_0(j),\iota_2(j))\\ \hline
0&(-49/200,-601/400)&(0,2)\\
1&(1/200,-601/400)&(1,2)\\
2&(51/100,-1/400)&(1,0)\\
3&(1/4,103/400)&(2,1)\\
4&(-49/200,-501/400)&(2,2).
\end{array}
\tag{6}
\]
It is strictly contained in \(K\).  Relabel the singleton coordinates as
\[
S=f_1,\qquad T=f_2.
\tag{7}
\]
Every \(B\)-edge is charging, so
\[
I_Z=I_W=\{{\sf S},{\sf T},0,1,2,3,4\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Both \(Z\) and \(W\) have the same bounded two-dimensional code:
\[
Z=W=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
\left(\frac{20003}{120800},0\right),
\left(\frac{203}{400},0\right),
\left(\frac14,\frac{103}{400}\right)
\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The selected support cycle is \(({\sf T},2,3)\), and the vertex
incidences in the order displayed in (9) are
\[
({\sf T},3),\qquad({\sf T},2),\qquad(2,3).
\tag{10}
\]
Every nonselected support slack is strict.  Thus neither code has an
active intrinsic slack, no rank-one, rank-two, or empty code occurs, and
\[
|Z|=|W|=\frac{4\,254\,209}{96\,640\,000},\qquad
D\mathscr C=D(|Z|-|W|)=0.
\tag{11}
\]

Order the eighteen coordinate columns as
\[
\begin{aligned}
(&a_{0x},a_{0y},a_{1x},a_{1y},a_{2x},a_{2y},
q_{0x},q_{0y},q_{1x},q_{1y},q_{2x},q_{2y},\\
&k_{0x},k_{0y},k_{1x},k_{1y},k_{2x},k_{2y}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
After suppressing identically zero chamber and defining-identity rows,
the complete nonzero canonical equality list is
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{\rm can}=\operatorname{rows}(&
DP_\varnothing,\ DQ_{12},DQ_{13},DQ_{23},DQ_{123},\\
&DR_1,DR_2,DR_3,DR_{12},DR_{13},DR_{23},\
D[(a_2-a_1),(q_1-q_0)]).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
The last row is the unique shared-fan row.  In sparse form, with omitted
coordinates equal to zero, these rows are
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
P_\varnothing&
a_{0x}:-1/4,\ a_{0y}:-1/4,\ a_{1x}:1/4,\ a_{2y}:1/4\\
Q_{12}&
q_{0x}:3/321602,\ q_{0y}:-101/32160200,\
q_{1x}:-151/16080100,\ q_{1y}:99/32160200,\
q_{2x}:-801/16080100,\ q_{2y}:-801/16080100\\
Q_{13}&
q_{1x}:-301/60400,\ q_{1y}:150901/18240800,\
q_{2x}:-1/60400,\ q_{2y}:99/18240800\\
Q_{23}&
q_{0x}:151203/4080400,\ q_{0y}:-99/40400,\
q_{1x}:1/400,\ q_{1y}:1/400,\
q_{2x}:3/20402,\ q_{2y}:-1/20200\\
Q_{123}&
q_{0x}:292027336310201/198151984920800,\
q_{0y}:-192943855459/392380168160,\\
&q_{1x}:-29072799193/19424760800,\
q_{1y}:726016020427/1466569440400,\\
&q_{2x}:-998752879599/99075992460400,\
q_{2y}:-586931086959/59249405392160\\
R_1&
k_{0x}:-12/7,\ k_{1x}:-2/7,\ k_{1y}:-2/7,\ k_{2y}:2/7\\
R_2&
k_{0x}:-2/7,\ k_{0y}:-2/7,\ k_{1y}:-12/7,\ k_{2x}:2/7\\
R_3&
k_{0y}:2/7,\ k_{1x}:2/7,\ k_{2x}:12/7,\ k_{2y}:12/7\\
R_{12}&
k_{0x}:-3/2,\ k_{0y}:-3/2,\ k_{1x}:-3/2,\ k_{1y}:-3/2\\
R_{13}&k_{0y}:3/2,\ k_{2y}:3/2\\
R_{23}&k_{1x}:3/2,\ k_{2x}:3/2\\
F&
a_{1x}:-1/50,\ a_{1y}:-1/50,\
a_{2x}:1/50,\ a_{2y}:1/50,\\
&q_{0x}:1/2,\ q_{0y}:1/2,\
q_{1x}:-1/2,\ q_{1y}:-1/2.
\end{array}
\tag{14}
\]
This exact matrix has rank \(11\).  There are no active containment
rows and no active intrinsic capacity rows, while the capacity row is
zero.  Hence
\[
G_{\rm can}=(0).
\tag{15}
\]

Choose \(a_r=a_0\).  It is a genuine unmarked vertex, it is not an
immediate event, and
\[
\Delta_0=[a_0-a_2,a_1-a_0]=\frac14=2|A_0|.
\tag{16}
\]
The release row is
\[
\mathcal R=
(1/2,1/2,-1/2,0,0,-1/2,0,\ldots,0)
=-2DP_\varnothing.
\tag{17}
\]
Therefore the exact canonical dual certificate is
\[
y_{P_\varnothing}=-2,\qquad
y_\alpha=0\quad(\alpha\ne P_\varnothing),\qquad
\lambda_{\mathscr C}=0.
\tag{18}
\]
In particular,
\[
\mathcal R=y^{\mathsf T}E_{\rm can}
-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G_{\rm can},
\qquad\lambda\ge0,
\tag{19}
\]
and, for every basis \(N\) of \(\ker E_{\rm can}\),
\[
\overline{\mathcal R}=\mathcal RN=0
\in-\operatorname{cone}\{\text{rows of }\overline G_{\rm can}\}.
\tag{20}
\]
Thus the universal canonical cone exclusion in the registered subgoal is
false.
